description:
ChunkReader selects chunks by name — covering_chunk_keys/2 takes the leading run of listed keys whose named max is at or above the target — and concatenates them oldest-first. It has no notion of one chunk subsuming another, so whenever a consolidated pack coexists with the constituents it replaces, every version in the overlap is delivered twice.

Add a monotonic filter to read_next_transaction/1: carry the last emitted version in the Stream.resource state (four clauses to update) and drop any entry at or below it.

The filter is version-level, never key-level. It discards a re-delivery of the same transaction; it never discards a later transaction that happens to touch the same key. It is safe because two copies of a version are always byte-identical — a pack's copy is a byte-copy of its constituent's, and chunks are already byte-identical across replicas by determinism — so the filter never chooses between two payloads.

read_all_transactions/2 has the same exposure and is unused outside its own tests: give it the same filter or delete it.

This is a DEPLOYMENT gate, not only a merge gate. Nothing may write a pack into an environment where this is not already running. IndexManager.apply_transaction/3 has no monotonicity guard, so duplicate delivery corrupts a materializer index rather than merely wasting reads.
title: ChunkReader: drop re-delivered versions so overlapping chunks read correctly
